keyEvents.impact: Inherited a Khartoum-centred state that marginalized its peripheries, seeding decades of civil war
Thirty years of Islamist military rule, international isolation and terrorism-sponsor designation

keyEvents.event: Darfur war and creation of the Janjaweed militias
keyEvents.impact: Genocide charges against Bashir; the Janjaweed later became the Rapid Support Forces
Lost three quarters of its oil output and much of its fiscal base
A fragile power-sharing deal left army and RSF as rival armed centres of power

keyEvents.event: Burhan and Hemedti coup ends the civilian transition
keyEvents.impact: Western aid and debt relief frozen; generals' rivalry set the stage for war

keyEvents.event: War erupts between the army (SAF) and the RSF on 15 April
keyEvents.impact: World's largest displacement crisis: over 12 million displaced and famine declared in Darfur

keyEvents.event: Army retakes Khartoum (March); RSF captures El Fasher (October) with mass atrocities
keyEvents.impact: De facto east-west partition: RSF and its Tasis parallel government hold Darfur from Nyala, the army holds the Nile valley and east

keyEvents.event: Kordofan becomes the main front; siege and drone war around El Obeid; Hemedti sentenced to death in absentia
keyEvents.impact: Truce plans from the US-Saudi-Egypt-UAE Quad stall while foreign drones and gold financing sustain both sides

history.narrative: A shattered state where a military junta in Port Sudan and Khartoum fights a former militia that rules Darfur as a rival government. Both survive on gold exports and foreign patrons, turning the country into a proxy arena for Egypt, Turkey, the Gulf monarchies and Russia's Red Sea ambitions.

redLines.description: International recognition of the RSF's parallel government or partition of Darfur
Continued Emirati arming and financing of the RSF
Loss of El Obeid, Port Sudan or the Nile corridor to the RSF

internalDivisions.name: RSF-held Darfur and western Kordofan (Tasis government) vs. army-held Nile valley and east
Arab pastoralist militias vs. Masalit, Zaghawa, Fur and Nuba communities
Islamist old guard and allied brigades vs. civilian pro-democracy movement

goals.description: Defeat or contain the RSF and retake Kordofan and Darfur
Cut off foreign arms and gold-smuggling lifelines sustaining the RSF
Restore Khartoum, revive gold and agricultural exports and avert famine
Win international recognition as Sudan's sole legitimate government
